scores.rationale: Several snippets directly support the stylized fact through the temperature-size rule (TSR), which states that many ectotherms reach smaller ultimate sizes at warmer temperatures. Snippet 3 explicitly defines the TSR (smaller sizes under warmer temperatures), and snippet 6 corroborates this with a reported negative correlation between temperature and size for ectotherms; snippet 11 references Bergmann's rule (larger sizes in cooler climates), which is consistent. One snippet (10) reports a contrary finding where warming increased mean body size, though the authors note this does not necessarily contradict the TSR. Most remaining snippets concern thermal performance, metabolic rates, and tolerance ranges without directly bearing on ultimate length responses to temperature. Overall the corpus offers moderate but clear support, predominantly corroborating the fact with only minor conflicting evidence.

snippets.title: From individuals to populations: How intraspecific competition shapes thermal reaction norms
snippets.label: supports
snippets.text: Abstract Most ectotherms follow the temperature‐size rule (TSR): in cold environments individuals grow slowly but reach a large asymptotic length. Intraspecific competition can induce plastic changes of growth rate and asymptotic length and competition may itself be modulated by temperature. Our aim was to disentangle the joint effects of temperature and intraspecific competition on growth rate and asymptotic length.

snippets.title: Heat resistance throughout ontogeny: body size constrains thermal tolerance
snippets.label: neutral
snippets.text: Abstract Heat tolerance is a trait of paramount ecological importance and may determine a species' ability to cope with ongoing climate change. Although critical thermal limits have consequently received substantial attention in recent years, their potential variation throughout ontogeny remained largely neglected. We investigate whether such neglect may bias conclusions regarding a species' sensitivity to climate change.
